newsitem.title: USA: Clinton "critical" for any tobacco settlement.
newsitem.headline: Clinton "critical" for any tobacco settlement.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton's support will be crucial for any settlement reached between the tobacco industry and anti-smoking forces, White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said Thursday.
White House Deputy Counsel Bruce Lindsey met Wednesday at the White House with Mississippi Attorney General Michael Moore and lawyers representing tobacco companies and plaintiffs suing the industry.
"We remain in contact with the parties," McCurry said, noting that "we do not have a specific formal proposal in front of the parties."
McCurry said the White House was monitoring the efforts to reach an out-of-court settlement in order to safeguard the administration's efforts to deter smoking by young people.

"I think the parties are well aware of the president's very strong views on the public health need of curbing tobacco use among young people, and they know that his support would be critical to any outcome that they seek," McCurry said.
"It would be difficult for legislation to pass Congress if it didn't have the president's support," McCurry said.
